title: Modders manage to port full DLSS 5 to AMD graphics cards from three generations
summary: The community has succeeded in running NVIDIA's full suite of upscaling technologies, including Multi Frame Generation, on officially unsupported Radeon hardware.

title: Two pallets with ZOTAC RTX 5090 graphics cards valued at $470,000 disappear at Brazilian airport
summary: The theft or loss of the high-end merchandise has been reported by multiple specialized hardware outlets and technology forums.

title: Sony warns PS6 component costs will exceed 700 euros in memory alone
summary: Industry analyses point to a final price above $1,000 due to rising RAM and storage costs driven by AI data centers.

title: Official DLSS 5 outperforms leaked version by 90% and reduces VRAM usage
summary: NVIDIA confirms the new neural network model processes workloads twice as fast and consumes 20% less video memory in non-natively supported games.

title: Anthropic allocates 5% of its shares to a public benefit trust
summary: The AI startup creates an independent fiduciary structure to prioritize safety and the common good over financial returns to investors.

title: MapQuest launches surveillance layer showing Flock camera locations on routes
summary: The feature allows drivers to see the location and orientation of automated license plate readers from multiple companies during navigation.

title: Meta acquires majority of Character.AI staff in mass hiring deal
summary: The tech giant absorbs the chatbot startup's talent without formally buying the company, securing key researchers for its AI models.

title: Anthropic proposes AI safety law that would only act after 50 deaths or $1 billion in damages
summary: The bill would make the Department of Commerce the sole regulator capable of halting an AI model, setting an extremely high intervention threshold.

title: Researchers train AI to detect concealed firearms using Wi-Fi signals
summary: The system analyzes disturbances in radio waves to identify hidden handguns without the need for cameras or physical metal detectors.

title: Meta admits its Ray-Ban smart glasses recorded conversations without user consent
summary: The company acknowledges the privacy flaw in its wearable devices and says it has implemented a fix following public complaints.
